name: Workflow Acceleration Toolkit
description: Led the development of a plugin suite, cutting down company's production time by 60%

items.label: Faster design system setup and configuration
Saved engineering costs through reduced handoff iterations

legend.style: Style Studio not only allows Designers to create and edit styles at scale, but also to export them for developers.
legend.sitemap: Site Mapper assists sales to create an interactive sitemap for fast navigation during stakeholder presentations.
legend.text: Text2Sheet allows managers to quickly export mockup text for client copywriting.

pain.headline: Understanding why mid-budget contracts were taking too long to produce
body: The company needed a way to shrink production time, without adding headcount or slowing down quality. We sat down with Design, Sales, Development, and PM to find out.
Four recurring pain points came up:
list: Design System colors and typography needed constant manual adjustment
Navigating prototypes during client presentations was clunky
Exporting tokens to development had no clear process
Pulling copy from mockups for the client copywriting doc was fully manual

source.headline: Every pain point traced back to the same file: Figma
body: The four different problems all shared one source: the Figma file. As a result, using Figma's plugins was the obvious direction, but the real question was how to structure it.

split.headline: I split the fix into three plugins, one per workflow
body: Bundling everything into a single tool would have dumped all the work on designers. Instead, I segmented by need and audience:
list: Style Studio: token & style management for Design
Site Mapper: prototype navigation for Design, Sales, and PM

tokens.headline: What do designers and developers actually need from tokens?
body: I worked directly with other designers to define the features we needed. We also benchmarked existing design systems and plugins to help make all the necessary features coexist in a coherent interface. I then exchanged with staff engineers to align token exports with their pipeline.

stat.label: Of front-end developers found the variable handoff inefficient

tokens.legend: We picked and compared needed functionalities from other plugins. We then defined what was working and what could be improved for each of them.

prototype.headline: Consultants didn't want to follow the prototype flow
body: They felt constrained by the flow, instead they wanted to jump straight to a specific page, or see only a limited subset of the prototype. For this case, the fix was pretty obvious: auto-generate a sitemap so any exposed page is one click away.

legend.before: At the time, consultants had to go through multiple pages to access the one they actually wanted to show.
legend.after: An interactive sitemap felt like the obvious solution as it would offer direct access to any pages.

copy.headline: Managers required a specific copywriting output
body: The text extractor tool was part of a broader automation system, as a result I worked closely with my manager to shape the CSV output for a downstream internal tool.

layout.headline: One layout didn't fit every element
body: Colors worked well shown as swatches, but fonts displayed the same way (i.e. small boxes) weren't convenient to adjust.
To answer this, we decided to switch the font to a full detail list so we could directly adjust fonts. However this layout made the list cumbersome to browse in the plugin's small window.
To offer flexibility, I decided to enable 2 layout options for colors and fonts, balancing quick scanning with precise editing.

legend.before: Before, all items were using a grid layout, which was efficient to clearly see the hierarchy, but not for editing fonts.
legend.after: After, we decided to introduce a list layout to directly be able to edit the font or see the color values.

tagging.headline: Tagging text one layer at a time didn't scale, we needed a faster flow
body: Text2Sheet's first flow required selecting and marking text layers individually which quickly became too slow for real projects.
To improve this, we adjusted the flow to auto-extract every text layer on a selected frame at once. Such feature required additional precautions like adding filters to keep the output manageable.
After trying the new flow, the manager's feedback was positive as it greatly reduced the workload, however this new flow unveiled other technical issues.

legend.before: Before, managers had to select texts one by one to add them to the export list.
legend.after: After, we realized a faster flow was to simply select the full frame, automatically add all the text and then filter them out.

latency.headline: The first-load latency for bigger project needed to be fixed
body: The plugin ran fine on small files, but slowed to a crawl past 10+ pages.
I rebuilt the storage layer to store only node IDs and load each tab's data asynchronously, instead of loading everything upfront.
The initial load time dropped from 12 seconds to 89 milliseconds.

stat.label: Faster loading time on larger projects

tab.headline: The initial tab bar made multi-level projects hard to navigate
body: For bigger projects with a lot of nested levels, the tab bar turned into an unreadable row, making it frustrating to find a specific tab.
I replaced it with an expandable tree view that mirrors the project's actual page hierarchy so navigating a multi-level project became straightforward again.

legend.before: Before, pages were flattened on a simple tab bar, which worked fine for 5-page projects, but it quickly became cumbersome.
legend.after: After, we decided to use a side tree view, which made multi-level websites much easier to navigate.

phasing.headline: Each plugin shipped in phases, timed to departments urgency
body: After exchanging with managers, I sequenced work one phase at a time rather than shipping everything at once.
Style Studio went first as design needed relief fastest for upcoming projects.
Site Mapper went between Style Studio's phases, since it was quick to build, and would leave some time to get Style Studio's first feedback.
Finally, Text2Sheet came last, since its impact on the process was the least significant.

ai.headline: AI was leveraged according to each plugin's complexity and deadline
body: Style Studio complexity required tighter control over the UI, so I designed key screens first and used AI as an assistant during development while maintaining key architectural decisions myself.
Site Mapper was simpler, so a quick design draft was enough to validate direction, then AI handled most of the build.
As the deadline was becoming tight for Text2Sheet, I skipped design entirely, vibe-coded a first release, and brought AI back in afterward to refactor it.

adoption.headline: A tool nobody understands doesn't get adopted
body: I wrote cross-department documentation covering not just the plugins, but Figma best practices in general. The document included comment conventions, client prototype sharing, and more.
We decided to combine it with live training sessions with each department to close the gap written docs couldn't.

results.headline: The toolkit sped up design production by 60% & reached 2,000+ users
body: It accelerated Design System adjustments from 1 hour to 20 minutes, made handoff faster by reducing the loopback between designers and developers by half, and community feedback kept improving it after launch, like including Figma's sections in the navigation map or supporting manual variables reload.

list.headline: Less over-engineering
list.challenge: Style Studio used Redux with async thunks for simple state management, more complexity than the plugin needed.
list.outcome: I now default to the simplest state model that works and scale up only when the data proves it's necessary.

list.headline: Giving greater attention to the adoption strategy
list.challenge: Style Studio's token workflow still needs hand-holding for junior designers less familiar with design systems.
list.outcome: I set in-app guidance (tips, hints, onboarding) and documentation as next phase priority.

list.headline: Rethinking the pipeline rather than a part of it
list.challenge: Text2Sheet fixed extraction, but it still sits inside a multi-tool export chain, which is why some PMs skip it entirely.
list.outcome: The next iteration would aim to centralize the export process into one tool.
